title: Relative Frobenius of a smooth proper curve has degree p to the n
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-pc-field-characteristic], and let $C$ be a smooth proper integral $k$-curve of dimension one [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For each integer $n\geq0$ put
$$C^{(p^n)}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k,\qquad \varphi_n(a)=a^{p^n},$$
with $k$-structure the second projection [def-pc-base-change]. Let $F_{C/k,n}:C\to C^{(p^n)}$ be the morphism with projections $F_C^n$ and the structure morphism of $C$, where $F_C$ is absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. For $n=0$, use the canonical identification $C^{(1)}\cong C$ and the identity morphism. Then $C^{(p^n)}$ is a smooth proper integral $k$-curve of dimension one, $F_{C/k,n}$ is nonconstant (it does not factor through a $k$-rational point), and its induced function-field embedding [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] has degree [def-pc-field-tower]
$$[k(C):F_{C/k,n}^*k(C^{(p^n)})]=p^n.$$

proof.text: Positive characteristic $p$ is prime: otherwise two nonzero smaller integer multiples of $1_k$ would multiply to zero. The binomial theorem in characteristic $p$ gives $(x+y)^p=x^p+y^p$, so $c\mapsto c^p$ is a unital ring homomorphism; its $n$-fold iterate is $\varphi_n(c)=c^{p^n}$. This is injective since $(x-y)^{p^n}=0$ implies $x=y$ in a field, and surjective since $T^{p^n}-c$ has a root in $k$. Thus $\varphi_n$ is a field automorphism, including $\varphi_0=\operatorname{id}_k$. Put $a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $K=k(C)$.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), first paragraph: elementary scalar Frobenius automorphism calculation over an algebraically closed field.

proof.text: Apply the automorphism-twist lift statement with $\sigma=\varphi_n$ and $u=F_C^n$. Its compatibility $au=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)a$ holds because ring homomorphisms preserve powers; $u$ is the identity on points by the definition of absolute Frobenius. The resulting twist is a smooth proper integral curve of dimension one, and the unique lift is $F_{C/k,n}$ by its two projection equations. The same statement gives nonconstancy, the injective generic-stalk pullback, and an isomorphism $\beta=\pi^*:K\xrightarrow{\sim}k(C^{(p^n)})$ with $F_{C/k,n}^*\beta=(F_C^n)^*$. The absolute-Frobenius definition makes the right side $x\mapsto x^{p^n}$ on generic stalks. Since $\beta$ is surjective, $F_{C/k,n}^*k(C^{(p^n)})=K^{p^n}$.

source.place: Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), definition and commuting diagram, and Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius); the generic-stalk calculation is written out.

proof.text: The smooth-curve p-basis statement applies to $C$ and yields the $K^p$-basis $(1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1})$ of $K$, so its degree over $K^p$ is $p$. Apply the Frobenius-image field-tower statement with $d=p$ and this basis. It gives $[K:K^{p^n}]=p^n$. Substituting the image from step 2 proves the stated degree. For $n=0$ both $\varphi_0$ and $F_C^0$ are identities, so the identity clause of the twist-lift statement identifies $F_{C/k,0}$ with the identity of $C$ and the tower formula gives degree $1$.
